outcomes.summary: LSD induced head-twitch responses normally in Y433F+/- mice (TrkB-binding mutant) but the response was blocked by 5-HT2A antagonist M100907, indicating HTR depends on 5-HT2A and is independent of TrkB binding.
outcomes.evidence: Head twitches in response to LSD occur normally in Y433F +/- mice but are blocked by M100907.

assays.assay_description: Repeated forced swim stress model with immobility measured; LSD administered as single dose and antidepressant-like effect assessed 7 days later in WT and Y433F+/- mice, with or without M100907 pretreatment.

application_type.evidence: Route not explicitly stated in available text.

setup_restrain.evidence: FST cylinder; per rubric, FST is classified as restraint.

food_restriction.evidence: Food not accessible in FST cylinder during recording.

water_restriction.evidence: Drinking water not accessible during FST.

time_to_assay.evidence: LSD produced a sustained antidepressant-like effect 7 days after a single administration.

sample_size.evidence: Sample sizes not reported in available manuscript text.

outcomes.summary: A single dose of LSD produced a sustained antidepressant-like effect (reduced immobility) 7 days post-administration in WT but not Y433F+/- mice. M100907 pretreatment did not block the effect, indicating it is TrkB-dependent but 5-HT2A-independent.
outcomes.evidence: LSD produced a sustained antidepressant-like effect 7 days after a single administration in WT but not Y433F +/- mice. Pretreatment with M100907 did not prevent the antidepressant-like effect of LSD.

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: Total immobility reported, not within-session time course.

B4_ethological.evidence: FST immobility explicitly excluded from ethological per rubric.

D1_continuity.evidence: Repeated sessions of the forced swimming test (rFST).

D2_session_duration.evidence: Session duration not explicitly stated in available text; standard FST sessions are typically <15 min.

D3_recording_days.evidence: Repeated FST sessions with antidepressant-like effect measured 7 days after LSD.

D5_followup.evidence: Antidepressant-like effect measured 7 days after a single LSD administration.

assays.assay_description: Contextual fear conditioning followed by extinction training; freezing behavior measured during extinction and recall at 3 days and 4 weeks after a single LSD injection in WT and Y433F+/- mice; control group tested for effect of LSD without extinction training.

application_type.evidence: Route of LSD not explicitly stated in available text.

setup_restrain.evidence: Mice freely move in conditioning chamber.

food_restriction.evidence: Food not present in conditioning chamber.

water_restriction.evidence: Water not present in conditioning chamber.

time_to_assay.evidence: Effects measured at 72 h and 4 weeks after a single LSD administration.

sample_size.evidence: Sample sizes not reported in available manuscript text.

outcomes.summary: A single LSD injection facilitated contextual fear extinction, reducing freezing at 3 days and 4 weeks post-administration in WT but not Y433F+/- mice. Extinction training was required; LSD alone without extinction did not reduce freezing.
outcomes.evidence: LSD also facilitates contextual extinction of conditioned fear response 72 h after a single administration, which persists for at least 4 weeks. However, these short- and long-term effects are lost in Y433F +/- mice. LSD alone does not bring about fear extinction, as extinction training is required to produce a sustained decrease in behavioral freezing after LSD treatment.

B4_ethological.evidence: Conditioned freezing explicitly excluded from ethological per rubric.

B6_cognitive.evidence: Fear conditioning/extinction requires associative learning and memory.

D1_continuity.evidence: Conditioning, extinction, and recall sessions on separate days.

D2_session_duration.evidence: Session duration not explicitly stated; standard fear conditioning sessions are typically <15 min.

D3_recording_days.evidence: Multiple recording sessions including conditioning, extinction, and recall at 72 h and 4 weeks.

D5_followup.evidence: Effects measured at 72 h and persist for at least 4 weeks after a single LSD administration.

judge_notes: All three candidates identified HTR, rFST, and contextual fear conditioning/extinction as the main behavioural assays; these were retained.

Added a fourth assay (monocular deprivation / ocular dominance plasticity) which is described in the text ('LSD also promotes visual plasticity and facilitates a shift in ocular dominance...') and was missed by all candidates; scored conservatively with low confidence on procedural details since methods detail is sparse in available text.

Dropped GLM's specific dose claims (0.2 mg/kg LSD, 2 mg/kg PSI) and i.p. route — these are not in the visible manuscript text and appear to be inferred/hallucinated; marked dosing as not_reported with low confidence.
For fear conditioning, used B6=1 (cognitive yes) as agreed by candidates; E6 scored 0 (single context chamber per session), overriding gptoss's score of 0 with 'Multiple zones' value mislabel.
Strain consolidated to reflect both WT (C57BL/6JRccHsd) and Y433F heterozygous (C57BL/6NTac-NTrk2em6006) lines used in the study.
